endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: Starting in 2025, EHR developers that supply Predictive DSIs as part of the developer’s EHR offering must disclose specific attributes and inform users if patient demographic, social determinants of health, or health assessment data are used in the Predictive DSI.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied tests whether disclosing source attributes of predictive decision support tools, including use of demographic and social determinants data, helps users judge validity or fairness. The recommendation currently rests on one guidance document that describes disclosure as a requirement for EHR developers starting in 2025.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Without comparative or observational data, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The support comes from a single guidance source, which reflects expert and policy judgment rather than measured effects on user decisions or patient outcomes.

The endorsing guidance states that, starting in 2025, EHR developers supplying predictive decision support must disclose specific attributes and tell users whether demographic, social determinants, or health assessment data are used. This framing suggests disclosure functions as a compliance obligation for developers, so health systems may receive these disclosures regardless of whether their effect on user judgment has been studied.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that measure whether clinicians and administrators read source-attribute disclosures, whether disclosure changes their decisions to adopt, trust, or override predictive tools, and whether it leads to detection of invalid or biased models before patient harm. Studies that document how often users currently lack this information would also help establish the size of the hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. It remains unknown whether disclosure of demographic and social determinants inputs helps users identify tools that perform differently for these groups.
